title: cost-opt: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: This PR centralizes default autotune recommendations for batching and KV-prefix caching, introduces model quantization profile plumbing for runtime selection, and ships the first iteration of unit-economics tooling used by product to estimate per-token cost impact. Motivation: Customers are often shipping with suboptimal defaults that increase cost by up to ~25% for common chat workloads. We need safe defaults + drift detection so we can reduce unit cost without regressions. What changed: 1) Defaults: added new config /runtime/defaults/batching_cache_defaults.go with conservative batch-sizing heuristics (adaptive target latency buckets) and prefix cache TTL defaults; these are opt-out for Dedicated/Private. 2) Autotune service: improved heuristics in optimizer/autotune/service.py to surface a recommended profile for low-latency and low-cost tiers, plus a migration path to apply per-route defaults. 3) Quant profiles: added model_registry/quant_profiles.yaml and runtime selection hooks in serving/runtime/quant_selector.go to prefer 4-bit profiles for supported models on GPU/TPU where accuracy tests pass. 4) UEcon tooling: shipped a small console service and CLI at tools/uecon that computes estimated per-token cost delta given batching/cache/quant choices; includes a CSV import for historical trace samples. 5) Tests & docs: integration tests for autotune in test/autotune and docs in docs/cost-optimization.md. Backwards compatibility: defaults are opt-out and gated with feature flags; existing customer pins remain honored. Performance: internal perf runs show median token-cost reduction of 18% on a representative chat trace with no statistically significant accuracy regression for models in our verified catalog. Rollout: feature-flag rollouts triggered; canary to 5% then 25% then global. Notes: this PR is a consolidation of several smaller changes in the cost opt epic and includes one refactor of the runtime config loader to support profile namespaces.

review_comments: Elena Martinez requested changes: Please add a unit test that verifies that the prefix cache TTL respects per-tenant overrides before falling back to the default - it's currently missing; also add an integration assertion for KV cache hit-rate metric.
Author (Aisha Patel) reply: Added test/integration/test_autotune.py and an extra assertion for metric prefix_cache.hit_rate > 0.1 in the canary runner. See commit f9b0c55.

Rohan Singh comment: The adaptive batching heuristic looks good but we should not aggressively default to larger batch sizes for latency-sensitive routes - added a suggestion to add route-level tags to opt into aggressive batching.
Author reply: Added feature flag gate and route tag opt-in (pkg/featureflags/flags.go). Updated docs to call out opt-in behavior.
Jonah Kim comment: Can we expose the UEcon CSV output format in docs for support to ingest traces?
Author reply: Added docs section and example CSVs under docs/examples/uecon_sample.csv.

Defaults are opt-out and gated behind feature flags. Expected median token-cost reduction ~18% for chat workloads with safe fallbacks.
